item: 1.30 — message timestamps: a time above the prompt and above the first reply text, and a date line where the day changes (2026-10-10)
branch: addUserMessage(text, imgs, ts) prepends a .ts line to the .turn (before the sticky .msg-user) and stamps data-day; sendTurn passes Date.now(), renderBlocks passes the record's ts. The first text .blk of a turn gets a .ts inside .turn-body (onStream text_delta, `turnStamped`; replay: the first assistant item after a user item). placeDaySeps() (50-blocks.js) re-lays .day-sep lines between #log's turns from data-day — called after a __transcript chunk and after renderEarlier's prepend; the live path checks the previous sibling turn. Labels: fmtClock / fmtDayLabel, factored out of fmtWhen (75-retraction.js).
provenance: Live `assistant` and `user` frames carry an ISO `timestamp` (taped 2026-08-12 wire captures in _local/); the typed prompt has NO wire frame, so its stamp is the page clock at sendTurn — this fixture therefore drives addUserMessage directly with a fixed instant (never sendTurn, which sends a real prompt over the bridge). Replay items are OUR shapes (SessionStore.Item.toJson, now with `ts` epoch ms — pinned Kotlin-side by SessionStoreTest). Stream frame shapes copied from fixture 89 / 19. Dates are built in-page with the local Date constructor so the expected labels hold in any timezone; the days are fixed past days (Oct 2026), so the label branch is always 'D Mon YYYY'. NEGATIVE CONTROL: RUN 2026-10-10 against the sandbox still serving the pre-change build (fixture written first): 5 passed / 11 failed / 0 aborts — every DISCRIMINATING assert failed ('absent' stamps, 0 .ts, '' day lines, 'turn' as the first log child); the passes are the GUARDs (turn / block counts) and the live no-day-line assert, which holds on both builds by construction. After the edit (JS + SessionStore `ts` + `./gradlew test` 169) and a sandbox restart: 16/16; with fixture 92, 38/38.
